case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.title: China Space Station x Starlink-1095

facts.text: Starlink-1095 maneuvered continuously between 16 May and 24 June 2021 down to an orbit of about 382 km, then stayed there.
On 1 July 2021 it had a close encounter with the China Space Station, which flew a preventive collision-avoidance maneuver.

aftermath.text: China notified the UN Secretary-General under Article V of the Outer Space Treaty (A/AC.105/1262).
China's foreign ministry said its emails to the US about the encounters got no reply.
The US told the UN that US Space Command did not estimate a significant collision probability and the events did not meet emergency notification criteria.

sources.label: China, note verbale to the UN Secretary-General, A/AC.105/1262 (3 Dec 2021)
United States, note verbale to the UN, 28 Jan 2022 (reported by SCMP)
Chinese foreign ministry: emails to the US received no reply (reported by Dawn/AFP)
Space.com: Tianhe dodged Starlink satellites twice in 2021

reality.basis: Reconstructed, not published: the cheapest station burn (prograde, about 18 h before TCA) that reaches Pc <= 1e-07 and a 1000 m miss, the same target the planner uses, so it is (up to the planner's 0.01 m/s rounding) a lower bound on what the station spent.

narrative.reality: On 01 July 2021 the crewed CSS (TIANHE) flew a collision-avoidance burn because STARLINK-1095 came close. There was no shared channel to agree who should move, so the station moved on its own. Our reconstruction puts that burn at 0.01 m/s and about 0.15 kg of propellant for a 44 t station. Months later, on 3 December 2021, China notified the UN; on 28 January 2022 the United States replied that the encounters did not meet emergency-notification criteria.
narrative.orbitSentinel: OrbitSentinel screens the pair, costs a burn for each spacecraft and lets each operator's agent state its case. The same avoidance flown by STARLINK-1095 costs 0.00035 kg, about 423 times less propellant than the station's burn. The mediator scores propellant reserve, maneuver cost, mission impact and delta-v (35/25/20/20) and recommends that STARLINK-1095 moves: 0.02 m/s retrograde, 0.00035 kg, giving 2.31 km separation. This takes seconds, and a human operator on each side approves before any command is sent.
narrative.brief: 2021: the station moved alone and the dispute went to the UN. With OrbitSentinel: STARLINK-1095 moves, using 423x less propellant. A human operator must approve any maneuver.

assumptions: Method: reconstruction from published altitudes/inclinations; no historical element sets were used (Space-Track GP_HISTORY needs an account). TCA, miss, Pc and covariance were never published.
TCA: 2021-07-01 12:00 UTC. Only the date (2021-07-01) is published; the time of day is an assumption.
Station orbit: circular, 390 km, i = 41.5 deg (UN note A/AC.105/1262).
Starlink orbit: circular, 382 km, i = 53 deg. Altitude: UN note (~382 km); inclination: Starlink shell-1 value, assumption.

Crossing geometry: relative RAAN is unpublished, so the crossing with the median relative speed over all RAANs is used (RAAN offset 270 deg, orbit-plane crossing angle 63 deg, relative speed 8.05 km/s). Assumption.

Covariance (1-sigma R/T/N position, metres): station (30.0, 300.0, 50.0), Starlink (30.0, 300.0, 50.0); order of magnitude for 1-2 day old orbits, assumption. Rotated into the encounter plane and summed: 363 x 42 m, angle 90 deg.
Starlink-1095 was holding station at ~382 km, so its orbit is modelled with the base covariance.
Hard-body radius: 30 m station + 5 m Starlink = 35 m (bounding spheres; assumption).

Miss distance: 1174 m along the covariance major axis, chosen so Pc = 0.0002 (just above the planner's 0.0001 burn threshold). The real value was not published and the US said its own Pc estimate was not significant, so this is the mildest event the planner would act on; burns below are floors, not worst cases.
Planning epoch 26 h before TCA (assumption); policy: Pc <= 1e-07, miss >= 1000 m, burn <= 5 m/s, as in app.physics.maneuver.

Station mass 43,980 kg = Tianhe + Tianzhou-2 (aft port) + Shenzhou-12 (crewed, docked 17 Jun-16 Sep 2021), using launch masses: Tianhe 22,500 kg, Tianzhou-2 13,640 kg (Wikipedia), Tianzhou-3 ~13,500 kg (state media), Shenzhou 7,840 kg (Wikipedia/spacefacts). Propellant and cargo used since launch are not subtracted.
Mass sensitivity: with Tianzhou at its 6,640 kg dry mass (36,980 kg total) the same burn would use 0.1257 kg instead of 0.1495 kg.
Station Isp 300 s: typical storable bipropellant (assumption; same value as the ISS in the live planner).

Starlink: 260 kg (SpaceX v1.x figure, space.skyrocket.de), krypton Hall thrusters, Isp 1500 s (not published; assumption). Burns are treated as impulsive, which understates a low-thrust electric burn that takes tens of minutes.
Costs: Tsiolkovsky equation via maneuver.propellant_kg, Clohessy-Wiltshire burn effects via maneuver.plan_maneuvers; propellant shown to 4 significant figures.

Burn sizes are rounded up to the planner's 0.01 m/s grid, so the smallest burn it can report is 0.01 m/s; the true minimum may be lower, and propellant for the cheapest options moves in steps of that size.

Published altitudes are approximate ("~"). The circular orbits are 8 km apart in radius, which alone would give a miss of at least that much, so the miss is imposed (see above) rather than derived from the elements.

Reality: the real station burn is not public. Modelled as the cheapest station burn that meets the planner's target (a lower bound, up to rounding). The real burn used an unknown lead time and margin.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: mediator
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: Screening shows CSS (TIANHE) and STARLINK-1095 passing 1.17 km apart at 8.0 km/s, collision probability 2.0 × 10⁻⁴. Both spacecraft can maneuver, so each operator should state its case before I score the options.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: agentA
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: No computed criterion favours STARLINK-1095 moving, so CSS (TIANHE) is ready to fly a 0.02 m/s prograde burn using 0.30 kg with 70% fuel in reserve, if the mediator agrees.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: agentB
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: No computed criterion favours CSS (TIANHE) moving, so STARLINK-1095 is ready to fly a 0.02 m/s retrograde burn using 0.00035 kg with 60% fuel in reserve, if the mediator agrees.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: agentA
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: We acknowledge your position. We will accept the mediator's scoring.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: agentB
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: We acknowledge your position. We will accept the mediator's scoring.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: mediator
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: CSS (TIANHE) moving: a 0.02 m/s prograde burn using 0.30 kg, miss 2.31 km, collision probability 6.7 × 10⁻¹¹. STARLINK-1095 moving: a 0.02 m/s retrograde burn using 0.00035 kg, miss 2.31 km, collision probability 6.5 × 10⁻¹¹. Weighted suitability: CSS (TIANHE) 59/100, STARLINK-1095 92/100. Decided mainly by maneuver cost and mission impact. Recommendation: STARLINK-1095 maneuvers, pending human approval.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: agentA
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: Agreed. CSS (TIANHE) keeps its current trajectory and will keep tracking STARLINK-1095 through closest approach, ready to re-screen if the maneuver slips.

case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.speaker: agentB
case-2021-07-01-css-starlink-1095.text: Understood. STARLINK-1095 will prepare a 0.02 m/s retrograde burn using 0.00035 kg, taking separation to 2.31 km. Submitted for human flight approval; no command has been sent.
